{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — License and Collaboration Agreement (CONFIDENTIAL)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer / "Ono")
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings and negotiation positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, **eight require action** (six deviations and two missing clauses) and **ten are compliant**, several of them at the fallback position rather than the preferred position.

The deal is, on balance, favourably structured for us on the points that matter most commercially: the licence grant is exclusive, sublicensable, extends to Affiliates and Third Party manufacturers and becomes perpetual and royalty-free on expiry (§ 2.1, § 13.1); there is no sourcing exclusivity, no minimum purchase commitment, no MFN burden, no employee non-solicit and no auto-renewal; the only liquidated-damages mechanic (§ 14.3) runs in our favour; and the arbitration regime seats disputes in Osaka when Array initiates (Art. XVII), which we should preserve.

The issues concentrate in risk allocation and exit. Two findings are **critical**: there is **no Array indemnity for Third Party IP infringement claims** on the very compounds, patents and know-how Array licensed to us, and § 11.4(a) affirmatively puts the cost of defending "Infringement Actions" on the Subject Party; and there is **no monetary liability cap anywhere in the Agreement**, leaving both parties with unlimited direct liability, including our broad product-liability and Article XV exposure. Four further **high**-severity items sit in walk-away territory under the playbook: joint IP that cannot be freely exploited (§ 11.1(c)–(d)), a post-termination non-compete tail on us alone with an unspecified duration (§ 8.2), the absence of any convenience right until after First Commercial Sale of both Products (§ 13.2), and — as missing clauses — the complete absence of any obligation on Array to return, export or delete our Data and Confidential Information (Art. X / Art. XIV). Medium items are an uncapped facility inspection right (§ 4.9(a)) and the lack of any conformance/GMP warranty on supplied Materials (Art. IX). Vendor insurance is missing but low severity and may be picked up in the separate Supply and Quality Agreements (§ 18.7).

---

## 2. Findings table

| Sev | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS (§ 16.2–16.4; cf. § 11.4(a)) | Two-way indemnity exists, but no Array indemnity for Third Party IP infringement/misappropriation claims on the licensed Products; § 11.4(a) puts defence costs on the Subject Party. Knowledge-qualified, Effective-Date-only Art. XV reps do not close the gap. Fails the fallback. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS (§ 16.5) | Mutual consequential-damages exclusion with carve-outs, but **no monetary cap of any kind** document-wide. Unlimited direct liability on both sides fails even the fallback. Mutual, so not walk-away. |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | PATENT PROSECUTION AND ENFORCEMENT (§ 11.1(c)–(d)) | Joint inventions are jointly owned but each Party is confined to internal-purpose practice, with licensing, enforcement and assignment gated on consent. Joint ownership without unrestricted exploitation is walk-away territory. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS (§ 8.2) | First sentence is a mutual, during-term, product-class restriction (acceptable). Second sentence is a post-termination non-compete on Ono only, running to an unspecified "[ * ]" anniversary and triggered even on our at-will termination. Fails the fallback (term only, 12-month cap). |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | TERM AND TERMINATION (§ 13.1–13.2) | At-will exit available only after the later of redacted anniversaries of First Commercial Sale of both Products; no convenience right through development, launch and early commercialisation. Notice period redacted. Walk-away territory. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § IV DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY ACTIVITIES (§ 4.9(a); cf. § 7.4) | Royalty audit in § 7.4 is at or above playbook. § 4.9(a) gives Array open-ended facility and records inspection with no frequency cap, notice period, cost allocation or confidentiality undertaking. Fails the fallback on frequency. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY (Art. IX; cf. Art. XV, § 15.4) | No warranty of conformity or quality for Materials Array supplies and no remedy anywhere; specifications deferred to future supply agreements. § 15.4 implied-warranty disclaimer leaves nothing carved out. Below the fallback. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION (§ 14.2) | Exit machinery is one-way: we transition studies, assign filings, hand over Data and Know-How and return/destroy Array's Confidential Information. No return, export, deletion or certification obligation on Array anywhere. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | GENERAL PROVISIONS (Art. XVI / Art. XVIII) | No insurance covenant anywhere; only incidental definitional references. Array manufactures, supplies and sponsors Clinical Studies and gives us product-liability and recall indemnities, so uninsured indemnity cover is a credit risk. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant (fallback) | GENERAL PROVISIONS (§ 18.9–18.10; § 4.5(b)) | Mutual, with the M&A carve-out we require; Affiliate assignment needs consent not unreasonably withheld or delayed — sits at the fallback. Change in Control mechanics run only against Array; no deemed-assignment trigger. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY (§ 9.4; § 2.1(b)) | No sourcing exclusivity: § 9.4(a) gives us "the right (but not the obligation)" to manufacture or subcontract, and § 2.1(b) grants a worldwide manufacturing licence extendable to Third Parties. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION (§ 14.3) | The only LD provision runs in our favour (royalty reduction on Array breach or data concealment). No Customer-payable penalty, termination fee or minimum; § 7.1 late interest is commercial, not penal. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant (preferred) | § II GRANT OF LICENSE (§ 2.1–2.2; § 13.1) | Exclusive/worldwide non-exclusive manufacturing licence, sublicensable to Affiliates without consent, extendable to Third Party manufacturers; not revocable at discretion; perpetual and royalty-free on expiry. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS (§ 18.3; Art. XVII) | New York substantive law (preferred). Forum is ICC arbitration rather than New York courts, but the seat is Osaka when Array initiates — the respondent-forum split favours us and we should not trade it away. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY | No MFN, best-price or third-party-matching obligation on us. The only comparable-terms language (§ 9.x(b)) runs in our favour on Subcontractor orders. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant (preferred) | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY (§ 9.1(a), 9.4) | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume cap. Array must supply our requirements; we retain the right but not the obligation to self-manufacture. Royalties on actual Net Sales. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | GENERAL PROVISIONS (§ 18.1–18.14) | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere; the integration clause prevents importing one from the 2016 Confidentiality Agreement. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | TERM AND TERMINATION (§ 13.1; § 14.4) | No auto-renewing term: a single Product-by-Product, country-by-country term to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, after which our licences are perpetual and royalty-free. § 14.4 confirms continued dealing is not a renewal. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips:

1. **Joint IP with no right to exploit (§ 11.1(c)–(d))** — co-ownership confined to internal purposes with a consent gate on licensing and enforcement. Our redline preserves the collaboration's joint-ownership architecture but restores an unrestricted right to practise, exploit and license co-owned IP, subject to the exclusive licences already granted, while retaining a consent gate on assigning a co-ownership interest.
2. **Post-termination non-compete tail on us alone (§ 8.2, second sentence)** — unspecified duration, triggered even where we terminate at will. Delete the tail; a 12-month tail with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs is an acceptable fallback.
3. **No convenience right for most of a multi-year term (§ 13.2)** — available only after the later of redacted First Commercial Sale anniversaries for both Products, with a redacted notice period we cannot verify against the 30-day preferred or 60–90 day fallback.
4. **No data return, export or deletion obligation on Array (Art. X / § 14.2)** — a one-way exit in which we hand over Data, Know-How and filings with nothing coming back.
5. **Unlimited facility and records inspection (§ 4.9(a))** — no frequency cap, notice, cost allocation or confidentiality undertaking.

The two critical findings (no IP infringement indemnity; no liability cap) are not classified as walk-away — the liability provision is mutual and the indemnity is two-way — but both fail the fallback on a material term and we should not sign without addressing them.

---

## 4. Next steps

**A. Redlines to issue (in priority order).** Each has been drafted as the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position:

| # | Section | Redline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | New § 16.2(e) | Add an Array indemnity for Third Party claims that the Products infringe or misappropriate Third Party IP, with customary modification and combination carve-outs, preserving the existing gross negligence / willful misconduct exception. |
| 2 | § 16.5 (appended sentence) | Add a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of twelve months' payments by Ono and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap (mirroring the existing 16.5 carve-outs) and our payment obligations excluded from the cap basis. |
| 3 | § 11.1(d) | Restore an unrestricted right for each Party to practise, exploit and license jointly-owned inventions, subject to the exclusive licences already granted; retain consent for assignment of a co-ownership interest. |
| 4 | § 8.2 | Delete the post-termination non-compete tail binding Ono, leaving the mutual during-term exclusivity intact. |
| 5 | § 13.2 | Convert to an at-will right exercisable at any time on thirty (30) days' notice, with pro-rata refund of amounts prepaid for post-termination periods. |
| 6 | New § 14.2(b) | Reciprocal transition obligation: up to six months' assistance at Array's then-current rates; return of our Data and Confidential Information within thirty days in machine-readable form; certified deletion thereafter — carved back for Data and Ono Know-How Array may retain under § 14.2(a)(iii) and (v). |
| 7 | § 4.9(a) | Add a once-per-Calendar-Year cap, thirty (30) days' prior written notice, Array-borne cost and a confidentiality undertaking; leave Array's on-site inspection right intact given the regulatory purpose. |
| 8 | New § 9.7 | Warrant that Materials conform to specifications and were Manufactured in accordance with GMP and applicable Law, with replacement or refund at Ono's election. |
| 9 | New § 18.15 | Array-only insurance covenant including products and clinical trial liability, with cyber cover conditional on Array handling our data, and certificates on request. |

**B. Fallbacks pre-authorised for the negotiator.** Non-compete: 12-month post-term tail with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. Convenience: 60–90 days' notice if Array needs transition runway. Audit notice: fifteen (15) days. Transition: data export within thirty days if certified deletion is resisted.

**C. Items to confirm rather than redline.** Obtain unredacted figures for the § 13.2 notice period, the § 8.2 post-term duration and the § 7.4 underpayment threshold before sign-off; classification of those provisions may change once the numbers are visible.

**D. Do not trade.** We should not redline Article XVII to exclusive New York court jurisdiction — doing so would surrender the Osaka home-seat protection that applies when Array initiates. Likewise, we leave untouched the provisions running in our favour: § 14.3 liquidated damages, § 9.x(b) comparable Subcontractor terms and the absence of any Array convenience right.

**E. Downstream documents.** Insurance limits and Materials specifications may be carried in the separate Supply Agreement and Quality Agreement contemplated by § 18.7; where they are, align rather than duplicate. Any minimum-order or firm-forecast terms should be resisted when the clinical and commercial supply agreements under §§ 9.3(a) and 9.4(b)(i) are negotiated, since no committed volumes are imposed here.

**F. Noted for the file, not flagged.** Consent (without an express reasonableness qualifier) for Third Party Sublicensees and distributors; consent for Affiliate assignment and no express bar on Array assigning to our competitor; "reasonable" rather than fixed notice under § 7.4; absence of a general Array gross negligence / willful misconduct indemnity limb; the non-refundable, non-creditable ¥3.5bn upfront licence fee (§ 6.1); our transition-cost responsibility under Article XIV and the § 8.2 restriction as soft costs of an at-will exit; and the inventorship-dispute forum carve-out in Article XVII."}
